text: huh thats i mean that all sounds correct to what it should be but the part of it that makes me scratch my own head is like i can import a model that is like 400k tris from a glb or obj and that also, when exported to a prop, is the same byte allocation ?
resolution: Question-only ask, no code changed. Confirmed and explained: yes, an imported 400k-tri GLB/OBJ pays the same uniform 20 B/vertex as any authored prop — there is no size- or source-based special casing. mesh_import.zig de-indexes GLB/OBJ into a non-indexed triangle soup (its documented output contract), so 400k tris = 1.2M verts = ~24 MB GPU-resident (was 38.4 MB pre-packing) for the ONE interned copy; placements stay 32 B refs; the cooked asset on disk stays raw f32 per V29. Pointed at the two levers for heavy imports: the existing import quality knob (decimateExpanded vertex clustering) and the roadmap item — an indexed-mesh pipeline that would recover the ~6x vertex sharing the de-index throws away (already noted at MAX_DYN_VERTS as the real long-term fix).
